I know it's not fashionable to talk about dreams, but my most vivid recurring dream (have been having it since young childhood) was witnessing a nuclear blast. It's always at some gathering. I step away from that gathering and go off by myself to do something or collect something. There is a moment where I stop and time slows down, I look off in the distance almost like I know something is coming, and boom. I see it go off. Pure terror. I can't move though. No sound will come out of my mouth when I try yelling for everyone else. I just see it and know its coming. I always wake up before the blast gets to me though.

It seems like a pretty painless way to go, given one is close enough to the center. There's a lot of bases around where I live, lots of drinking water. I imagine the PNW would be a prime target in such a conflict.

It's tough because survivability can be really variable, not to mention we don't have that much real-world evidence to look at where humans were exposed to the blasts.

In the Hiroshima explosion (only a 16 or 17 kt bomb), one of the famous survival stories was of a woman 300 m from the hypocenter. She was in a steel-reinforced concrete building and hid behind the desk. She survived and had only minor injuries. But people outside of the same building got smoked. So just being indoors has a huge impact.

If we're talking about a 20 MT bomb, it's all out the window. You could get third degree burning 20 miles from hypocenter with a bomb that big.

If I were going to be victim to that explosion, I'd basically want to be right beneath it. If you were at immediate hypocenter, you'd be vaporized before you even knew what was happening. We're talking temperatures in the millions for a brief moment in time. Even at a distance of 1000 ft from center, you'd be dead in a matter of 1 or 2 seconds max. You'd get burned immensely, but the shock wave from the blast would hit you in about 2 seconds and that would be that. So a brief moment of suffering. It would be much better than being 5 or 10 miles out and just getting flash burned but possibly shielded from the concussive death.
